To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
feeding a coarse diet with butyric acids improves performance and gut development in broilers fed a poorly digestible rapeseed protein source.

a coarse diet with a poorly digestable protein source and supplemented with BA improved the FCR of broilers, and the negative effects of a poor protein digestibility can partly be counterbalanced by coarseness of diet and BA supplementation.
the inclusion of BA improved the feed conversion ratio and the villus height:crypt depth ratio in broilers fed a poorly digestible rapeseed meal-based diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for the optimization of diet structure, fermentable carbohydrates, and butyric acid in broiler diets with a poorly digestable protein source.
the effects of dietary coarseness, BA supplementation, and FC supplementation in a poorly digestable protein source on broiler performance and gut morphology and fermentation.
the effect of dietary coarseness, BA, and FC on growth performance, gut morphometry, and cecal digesta fermentation in broilers fed a RSM-based diet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coarseness of a diet supplemented with BA improves performance and gut health of broilers fed diets containing poorly digestible protein sources.
the coarseness of a diet containing a poor quality protein source, supplemented with BA, improved the performance of broilers, whereas supplementation with FC did not.
a coarse diet, with or without BA supplementation, is a promising approach to improve growth performance of broilers in the presence of poorly digestible diets based on RSM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

coarse grinding of a diet containing a high proportion of RSM and BA supplementation improves the performance of broilers by enhancing the digestibility of the diet and reducing the negative effects of a high concentration of BCFA and spermine on gut development and growth performance.
a coarser structure of a diet containing a poor protein source can be improved by the addition of BA and FC.
a coarse, BA-supplemented diet can be used to counteract the negative effects of poorly digestible protein in broiler diets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coarse grinding and BA can improve the performance of broilers when a poorly digestible source of protein is used.
the inclusion of coarse feed ingredients in broiler diets can be a useful strategy to improve performance of broilers, especially when fed diets based on poorly digestible protein sources.
the use of a coarse diet supplemented by BA is a practical and cost-efficient strategy to improve the growth performance of broilers.
